applicability: Classifying foot slip in later articulated experiments using post-step contact-point motion
Bounding the usable static-friction budget for the canonical lab floor and material pair
Detecting instrumentation bugs where a held contact is misreported as sliding
claim: For the exact L1.1 4 kg free sled on a flat static floor with equal authored friction 0.6, rough=false, zero bounce, and 60 Hz Jolt physics, a monotonic staged central force ramp 0-40 N last completes a hold at 22 N and first completes a slide at 24 N, giving an empirical breakaway-to-normal ratio bracket of 0.56101-0.61230 around the approximately 39.2 N predicted normal load. Contact-relative velocity captured inside _integrate_forces behaved as a pre-constraint candidate equal to the one-tick free acceleration F*dt/m while post-step displacement and velocity stayed exactly zero, so slip classification must use reconstructed post-step contact-point motion v_point = v_com + omega x (p - c), never the callback candidate.

evidence.certification_claim_boundary: This campaign can certify only the L1.0-L1.7 contact-engine observations named by the exact source-pinned programs. L1.8 and the knowledge guard are supplementary constraints. It establishes no articulated load-bearing limb, standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, walking, accepted knowledge, automatic creature guidance, or per-foot allocation of reconstructed whole-system load.

programs.claim_scope: Tangential slip observation and breakaway bracketing fail closed on invalid evidence.
The finite-friction sled brackets hold, breakaway, and sliding under its declared ramp.

failure_boundaries: Does not cover other friction values, materials, rough surfaces, or nonzero bounce
Does not cover moving counterparties; a moving ground must supply its own measured post-step point velocity instead of inheriting zero
Does not cover articulated bodies, joints, motors, or any actuated limb
Does not establish standing, bracing, fall arrest, getting up, or walking
mechanism: Godot exposes a predicted contact impulse, and impulse divided by step time is a step-average solver-load estimate rather than an exact continuous force. The integrate-forces callback samples velocity before the constraint solve, so a successfully friction-held contact still reports the unconstrained one-tick velocity candidate. Post-step body state is the solved authority, so contact-point motion reconstructed from post-step center-of-mass and angular velocity separates held contacts from sliding contacts.
